facts.claim: AOC Chablis first recognised by decree of 13 January 1938
facts.source: INAO, cahier des charges AOC Chablis (modification draft, opposition 23 June 2025), I

facts.claim: Geographical area: 17 communes of the Yonne department
facts.source: INAO cahier des charges IV.1; Open Wine Atlas details-fr.json communes (17)

facts.claim: The Serein valley, a tributary of the Yonne
Wines made exclusively from Chardonnay B
facts.source: INAO cahier des charges V; Open Wine Atlas grapes for Petit Chablis, Chablis, Chablis Grand Cru

facts.claim: Marls with Exogyra virgula (Kimmeridgian marls) in the relief
facts.source: INAO cahier des charges X.1.a, X.1.b

facts.claim: Fairly high risk of winter and spring frost ('un assez fort risque de gelées hivernales et printanières')
Terrain e=[119,210,327,164,257] m: min 119, mean 210, max 327; relief 208 m
facts.source: Open Wine Atlas terrain stats (details-fr.json fr-inao-a146)

facts.claim: Bedrock: 93% carbonate sedimentary rocks (limestone, marl, dolomite)
Chablis Grand Cru: 7 climats (Blanchot, Bougros, Grenouilles, Les Clos, Preuses, Valmur, Vaudésir); delimited area 106.6 ha
facts.source: Open Wine Atlas (INAO delimitation data: fr-inao-a147 area_ha, vineyards d440-d446); Open Wine Atlas Study lesson 'Chablis and the Grand Auxerrois'

facts.claim: Grands crus share one hillside on the right bank of the Serein, facing the town
facts.source: Open Wine Atlas Study lesson 'Chablis and the Grand Auxerrois'

facts.claim: Four levels: Petit Chablis, Chablis, Chablis Premier Cru, Chablis Grand Cru, all Chardonnay
facts.source: Open Wine Atlas Study lesson; Open Wine Atlas appellation data (INAO)

facts.claim: Annual precipitation Chablis 740.3 mm vs Paris-Montsouris 634.3 mm (1991-2020)
64.6 days a year with Tn <= 0 °C at Chablis; April 5.3, May 0.5
July mean max 27.2 °C, mean min 13.2 °C at Chablis
WSET bands: cool up to about 16.5 °C growing season average
facts.source: Open Wine Atlas study lesson 'Climate and weather' (used in earlier episodes)

facts.claim: Early-budding Chardonnay is most exposed to spring frost; Chablis protects buds with heaters, wind machines and sprinklers
